type_hypothesis.against: Her own self-description leans Two: "the classic do-gooder" (C04), "a supportive manager. I really want people to succeed" (C14), "in my heart ... a people leader" and "an expert in people" (C56), and she entered international development partly to understand Dario's interests (C10). OpenAI colleagues saw her as the "high-EQ counterpart" (C17); she invests in the sibling bond (C26). Several observations cut against a harsh, rigid One: she is easy about her own mistakes (C31), sidesteps a mistakes question rather than self-criticizing (C115), excuses doctors who misdiagnosed her (C67), left Capitol Hill as "slow and bureaucratic" (C05, C86), retired a value because not everyone loved it (C60), prizes changing one's mind and moral pluralism (C61), and declines to arbitrate disputes outside her expertise (C16). She shows no first-person anger in roughly 20 hours of her own speech and named no trigger when asked (C58). The anger evidence (C19-C21) is reported by interested or unnamed parties, and the WSJ shows the Brockman exclusion was Dario's position first, so loyalty to her brother explains it as well as a standard. Much of the One material is also a president's job: building feedback systems, culture interviews and values is what an operator does. Her "right thing" vocabulary is shared with Dario (C73).
type_hypothesis.alternative_case: Type 2 is the strongest rival and was the held, low-confidence hypothesis of the 2026-10-06 run. Its case: she chose her first field to be near Dario's interests (C10); she stands beside a star and translates his vision (C12, C112); her consistent self-identity from 2022 to 2026 is helper, supportive manager and people leader (C04, C14, C56); colleagues saw her as the warm one (C17); she tends the bond with Dario and protects family time (C26); her account of joining OpenAI includes wanting to "help" good people who were "a little bit of a mess" (C43). The reported OpenAI conflicts could be a Two defending her brother and her people (C19, C21). Why it loses on the current record: under cost she moves toward a standard rather than toward approval or relationship (C48, C49, C29); she builds impersonal rules and applies them to herself (C50, C51); she rejects being indispensable (C57), the opposite of a Two's need to be needed; she treats flattery of users as the hardest defect to "stamp out" and wants Claude's warmth "approachable, but distant" (C49, C39); and close colleagues credit her with "keeping the bar high," not with care (C55). Other types: Six (doubt and fear of loss in C27, "no surprises" in C59, mentor counsel in C23 and C116) is weakened because her fear centers on being wrong ("Are we accidentally making things worse?") and she acts decisively; Nine (meeting Dario in the middle in C62, refusing to arbitrate in C16, public diplomacy in C24, C44) fails on the reported friend-blocking and point-by-point rebuttal and on her readiness to judge conduct in C45 and C66; Three is not supported: she moves from status to standards when offered front-runner framing (C63).
type_hypothesis.discriminator: What she does when a principle costs her something, and what she says she was protecting. Across 2021-2026 and at least six venues, her own accounts of costly choices cite what was right or honest (Pentagon red lines, no ads against investor pressure, turning away customers rather than selling "a bill of goods": C48, C49, C29), and she never cites protecting Dario, her staff or her own standing (C106, C113). Her signature management acts are impersonal standards applied to everyone including herself (the 2021 feedback matrix with tracked completion, board reviews that include her and Dario, zero tolerance for going behind backs: C50, C51, C52), and she wants out of any job where she is indispensable (C57). A Two under cost would move toward relationship, approval and being needed; she moves toward the rule. In the one joint conversation where both siblings judge OpenAI, she asks whether its choice was "principled" or "opportunistic" and Dario softens it (C45), which also separates her One from his Six. Limits: her "right thing" vocabulary is shared house language and is discounted (C73); the reported OpenAI conflicts (C19-C21) corroborate but cannot anchor; no named colleague yet describes her reaction when someone cuts a corner.
type_hypothesis.unexplained: Why a self-identified "people leader" whose reports call her supportive became, in two independent but unnamed-source accounts, the hard-edged process enforcer and negotiator of the OpenAI split; how a high bar coexists with genuinely relaxed self-mockery about her own errors (C31) and charity toward others' errors (C67); why she followed Dario into her first field (C10) if her compass is principle rather than attachment; how much of the public warmth and of the public rigor is temperament versus the operator role Anthropic needs beside Dario; and the near-total absence of first-person resentment in a large record, which a One reading must treat as control or privacy rather than proof.
